name: Buffoon
flavor: The bit is that you will not stop. They hit you, you get up, you make the joke again. Eventually it stops being funny for them. The Buffoon is the Jester who keeps the company upright — the only source of true healing anywhere in the circus.

features.name: Take the Fall
features.description: When an attack **hits** an ally within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to get in the way. This resolves after the attack has already hit: **nothing is re-rolled and your own AC never comes into it** — the blow was always going to land, and you are only deciding who it lands on. You take the damage in your ally's place, and you take **half** of it. Because your reaction is spent doing this, you cannot Parry the same blow, and this never counts as a Parry.
features.sheetSummary: Reaction, 10 ft. When an attack hits an ally you take it instead, at HALF damage. Its requirements and how it resolves are listed below.
features.narration: You do not push anybody. You could not shift the strongman if you tried, and you have never once got there in time. What you do is trip — a beautifully judged, entirely deliberate accident that puts you in the path with your feet already going out from under you. The blow catches you on the way down instead of square on, and you ride it into the floor, roll through it, and come up talking. It is the oldest thing you know how to do: you have been falling over professionally since you were nine, and the whole craft of it is that the floor never gets you as hard as it should.

options.name: You must see the attacker
options.effect: You cannot intercept a blow you never saw coming.

options.name: Something physical only
options.effect: An attack roll dealing physical or fire damage. Never a saving-throw effect, and never psychic damage even from an attack roll — there is no trajectory to step into.

options.name: The hit has already landed
options.effect: You do not re-roll the attack and it is not compared to your AC. The damage is rolled once and you take half of it, rounded down; your ally takes none.

options.name: It costs your reaction
options.effect: You cannot also Parry that blow, and this never counts as a Parry. Any damage reduction you have applies to your half as normal.

features.name: Rubber Bones
features.description: You have been thrown off more stages than you can count. You have resistance to bludgeoning damage from falls, collisions, and being thrown, and whenever you are knocked prone you can stand up for 5 feet of movement instead of half your speed.
features.sheetSummary: Resistance to bludgeoning damage from falls, collisions, and being thrown. Standing up from prone costs 5 ft of movement instead of half your speed.
features.narration: Same trick, all the time, whether anybody threw anything or not. You go down the way a dropped coat goes down — loose, folding, nothing locked — and the ground takes almost nothing off you. Getting back up is the easy half; you have never once had to think about it.

features.name: Beneath Contempt
features.description: Nobody guards their tongue in front of the fool. Guards, servants, courtiers, and hired muscle routinely discuss things in front of you that they would never say to an armed stranger, and you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks made to be dismissed as harmless. A creature that has already seen you do something dangerous is immune to this for as long as it remembers.
features.sheetSummary: Guards, servants and hired muscle speak freely in front of you. Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks made to be dismissed as harmless. A creature that has seen you do something dangerous is immune to this for as long as it remembers.
features.narration: They look straight through you and carry on the conversation. You are furniture that occasionally makes a noise, and you have built an entire career out of what people say in front of furniture.
